A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Selective Prompt Anchoring study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable; v6 retains Appendices A–L and adds Appendix M.

before.justification: v5 reports original attention analyses, code-generation experiments, ablations and computational-cost measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark accuracy, attention analyses and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix M adds a confidence-modulated variant: each candidate token receives weight ω_t = λ(1 − p_t), applied elementwise to the logit difference. This changes one weighting component while retaining the existing masking and logit-combination framework; no evaluation of the variant is reported.

E1.justification: The code benchmarks, five-language HumanEval-X evaluation, and TruthfulQA, GSM8K, MMLU and BoolQ evaluations are retained. Appendix M introduces no evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same base models and methods, including PASTA, Self-Debugging, Self-Edit, Self-Planning and ReAct. The new adaptive variant is not added to any reported comparison.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, decoding settings and five-fold tuning remain unchanged. The all-task activation and tuning explanation removed from Section 5.6 remains in Appendix J; this does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: Anchored-text ablations, prompt-length and anchoring-strength analyses, transferability tests, and code examples are retained. Appendix M proposes improved stability without adding a robustness test or ablation.

E5.justification: Five-fold averaging and Appendix J.1's tuning-variance reporting are unchanged. Appendix M's confidence refers to token probabilities used by the method, not additional statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The matched tables, plotted findings and code examples retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B's HumanEval Pass@1 as 75.6% without SPA and 88.5% with SPA in both versions. Appendix M adds no measured outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix M introduces Equation 21, formally defining probability-dependent token weights and the vocabulary-wide weight vector. Existing Equations 1–20 and their derivations remain unchanged; no new proof accompanies the definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central attention-dilution, SPA and performance claims, including the reported improvement of up to 12.9%. The adaptive extension is introduced outside these core contribution statements.

C2.justification: Appendix M adds the rationale for adjusting high-confidence candidates less and low-confidence candidates more, with the stated aim of improving stability and avoiding tuning. Existing result interpretations and Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation, quantization, hardware, prompt formatting and code/package access disclosures are retained. Appendix M provides a method definition but no chosen λ value or additional implementation settings.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and substantive positioning against prompting, attention-steering and logit-arithmetic methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 5.6 is locally rewritten, introduces the adaptive variant and references the new Appendix M. Minor capitalization edits accompany this addition; the existing narrative and section order are largely retained.

P2.justification: The same six figures and seventeen tables are retained, with minor figure-rendering differences and appendix reflow. Existing displays move relative to surrounding text, notably Table 11 from page 21 to page 22; no new display is added.

improvement.justification: v6 adds an explicit adaptive-strength proposal, but provides neither evaluation of its intended stability and tuning benefits nor a value or selection rule for λ. Existing empirical evidence is unchanged, and Section 7 still describes fixed strength as a limitation. The extension's net contribution to overall paper quality therefore remains uncertain.
